summary: Iteration 4 — Backend validation of the refactored Mesure model (9 new optional fields: bay_height, bay_width, bay_diagonal, floor_reserve, bloc_thickness, wall_type, insulation_thickness, finish_outer, finish_inner) + legacy field backward-compat + updated PDF/JSON exports. 74/74 pytest tests pass: 11 new iter4 tests + 63 regression tests from iter1/iter2/iter3, all green with zero modifications to existing tests or backend code.

minor.issue: wall_type has no backend enum validation — arbitrary strings like 'foobar' are accepted and persisted. Per iter4 spec this is expected (frontend enforces 'ite'|'iti'|'crepi_simple'), but consider adding server-side validation in a future iter for defense-in-depth.

compute_alerts only inspects legacy fields (width_*, height_*, diag_*). When only new bay_* fields are supplied, alerts=[] silently — documented expected behavior, but worth flagging: no faux-aplomb detection on bay_height/bay_width yet.
Carry-over from iter2/iter3: still does NOT filter by company_id (only matches by id); export.json correctly does. Cross-tenant PDF download possible by UUID guess.
Carry-over: silent 200 no-op when id is unknown.
Carry-over: returns 200 instead of REST-conventional 201 on POST.
Carry-over: 'module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' on startup. Functional but noisy.

action_items: (Optional) Add server-side enum validation for wall_type ∈ {ite, iti, crepi_simple} to mirror the frontend constraint.
(Optional) Extend compute_alerts to also flag inconsistencies in bay_diagonal vs sqrt(bay_height^2+bay_width^2), and a faux-aplomb proxy if/when multiple bay measurements are introduced.
(Optional carry-over) company_id filter on export.pdf; 404 on delete-not-found; 201 on creation; pin bcrypt<4.
critical_code_review_comments: MesureCreate cleanly extended with 9 optional new fields — no breaking change. Legacy fields kept Optional, so unmodified iter1/2/3 payloads still pass Pydantic validation (verified by 63/63 regression tests).

compute_alerts is unchanged and references only legacy fields — when new-only payloads are sent, alerts=[] which is the documented expected behavior. No crash on missing legacy values (already Optional).
POST /api/mesures uses payload.model_dump() then merges id/created_at/alerts/slope, so new fields are persisted verbatim and returned by both list_mesures and export.json (verified).

PDF builder (server.py L611-643) lists the 9 new fields FIRST (Hauteur baie, Largeur baie, Diagonale, Réserve Sol Fini, Épaisseur Bloc Béton, Épaisseur Isolant, Finition ext, Finition int, Type paroi) then legacy. wall_type is mapped to human labels ('ITE'/'ITI'/'Crépi simple') with fallback to raw string — robust against arbitrary values.
Fields with value None are skipped from PDF rows — clean output for mixed payloads. Verified export.pdf returns 200 + application/pdf + valid %PDF- magic header with new-fields-only mesure.
Role gating unchanged: technician CAN POST /api/mesures with new fields (verified test_technician_can_post_with_new_fields).
No MongoDB _id leakage — all find() calls already project {_id:0}.
seed_data_creation: One ephemeral chantier 'TEST_Iter4Client' created via commercial token at module-fixture setup, populated with ~7 TEST_-prefixed mesures across new-only, legacy-only, mix, wall_type variants, and a technician-authored mesure. Teardown deletes the chantier as admin which cascades mesure cleanup via existing DELETE /api/chantiers/{id} handler. Demo users and 5 seeded chantiers untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend iter4 is fully green (74/74). All 9 new MesureCreate fields validated end-to-end: POST acceptance, GET list retrieval, export.json shape, export.pdf 200 + %PDF- bytes. Backward compatibility verified (legacy-only payloads still work, mixed payloads still produce alerts from legacy values). wall_type has NO server-side enum check — only the frontend enforces ite/iti/crepi_simple. compute_alerts intentionally still references legacy fields only (new-only mesure → alerts=[]). Next iteration likely needs frontend testing of the 3-step wizard: (1) block picker, (2) raw-bay H/W/D/floor_reserve form (mandatory), (3) bloc thickness + wall_type segmented + indicative insulation/finish fields. Watch for keyboard handling on numeric inputs and testID coverage on segmented controls.
rca_of_issue: No issues observed. Zero code or test changes were required to existing files — the iter4 refactor is purely additive at the model level and the PDF builder gracefully iterates new fields first, legacy second, skipping None values.
